goals.title: Select the relevant inventory
goals.concept: Inventory type and time context determine which infrastructure entities are comparable.
goals.narration: Show the inventory at the entity level that owns the reported resource.
goals.reasoning: The correct entity level prevents host, container, and service signals from being conflated.
goals.evidence: The inventory shows the scenario entities.

demonstration.narration: I'll open the ${var.inventory} inventory so we're comparing the same kind of entity when looking for an outlier.
demonstration.reasoning: Hosts, pods, containers, and services describe different ownership levels. Comparing like entities gives us a meaningful baseline.
demonstration.evidence: The inventory now lists comparable entities at the ${var.inventory} level. We can look for an outlier in the next view.

hints: Choose the entity level that owns the reported resource.
Use the Infrastructure inventory's Show selector.
Select ${var.inventory}; Show me can demonstrate it.

goals.title: Show the metric behind the symptom
goals.concept: Colouring every entity by one metric makes an outlier visible against its peers.
goals.narration: Colour the inventory by the resource metric that matches the reported symptom.
goals.reasoning: An overall health average can hide one saturated entity; one metric across all of them shows it.
goals.evidence: Every entity is now coloured by the chosen metric.

demonstration.narration: I'll colour the inventory by ${var.metric}, the resource that matches the reported symptom, so an outlier stands out against its peers.
demonstration.reasoning: An overall health average can hide one saturated or imbalanced entity. Showing one metric across every entity makes the comparison direct.
demonstration.evidence: Every entity is now coloured by ${var.metric}. One of them should stand apart from its peers; that is the one to select next.

drifts.note: You chose ${action.value}; check whether that resource is the one the report describes.

hints: Match the metric to the symptom in the brief.
Select ${var.metric}; Show me can point to it.

goals.title: Select the entity that stands out
goals.concept: Peer comparison reveals the outlier that aggregate health hides.
goals.narration: Select the entity that stands apart from its peers on that metric.
goals.reasoning: The abnormal entity must be compared with healthy peers or an earlier period.
goals.evidence: The selected entity's detail shows the metric that stood out.

demonstration.narration: I'll select the entity that stands apart from its peers to open its detail.
demonstration.reasoning: One entity's colour isn't proof yet; its detail shows the metric over time against the incident window.
demonstration.evidence: ${truth.finding} stands apart from its peers on ${var.metric}. Treat it as a hypothesis until another signal corroborates its timing.

hints: Compare the entities' colours: one should stand apart.
Click the entity in the inventory to open its detail.

drifts.note: You selected ${action.value}; check whether it really stands apart from its peers.

goals.title: Correlate supporting evidence
goals.concept: Resource correlation is stronger when the timing aligns with a restart, log, or latency event.
goals.narration: Open supporting metric detail or correlated logs.
goals.reasoning: Correlation checks that the resource pattern aligns with observed impact.
goals.evidence: The supporting record contains the corroborating scenario fact.

demonstration.narration: I'll open the outlier's detail and related logs at the same time to see whether the resource change lines up with the reported issue.
demonstration.reasoning: A resource spike alone does not prove customer impact or causation. Matching its entity and timing to another observable signal tests the relationship.
demonstration.evidence:
The supporting record should align with the outlier’s entity and time.

That independent correlation turns the metric pattern into evidence for the conclusion: ${truth.conclusion}

goals.evidence: The response cites the metric and correlation.
